settings.text:
The Nobel Prize for Chemistry was awarded in 1996 to scientists Kroto, Smalley, and Curl for the discovery of fullerene C60. Along with graphite and diamond, fullerene C60 is one of the eight allotropic forms of carbon.

It has icosahedral symmetry of the Fibonacci type, identical to the symmetry that is present in healthy, functional biological structures, natural phenomena, and throughout the universe, which, according to Plato, has dodecahedral symmetry. This groundbreaking discovery opened up a completely new chapter in the application of such a uniquely symmetric quantum nanomaterial in nanomedicine, overall healing, and life-extending properties.

settings.text: Your eye is equipped with structures that protect it from some kinds of light. Your cornea and lens protect the light-sensitive retina at the back of your eye from damaging UV rays, for example. Those structures don’t keep out blue light. Continuous exposure to harmful radiation irreversibly damages our eyes, causing cataracts and macular degeneration. Light exposure also adversely affects brain function and general physical health.
